title: Where meanings converge and diverge: Revisiting linguistic relativity across 81 languages
abstract: arXiv:2610.30778v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Do people who speak different languages organize concepts in similar ways? This question lies at the heart of the Sapir--Whorf hypothesis and debates about linguistic relativity. Shared basic meanings, however, need not imply shared relations among them. We compared relations among 196 basic concepts across 81 languages, using word embeddings from two multilingual models to quantify conceptual structure expressed in language. Cross-language correspondence was greater for sociocultural meanings than for meanings concerning nature and motion, a contrast recurring across models and classifications. Within the sociocultural domain, relational differences increased with geographic separation; less closely related languages differed more across all domains. translated_title: 意义汇聚与分歧之处：跨81种语言重新审视语言相对论
translated_abstract: 说不同语言的人是否以相似的方式组织概念？这个问题处于萨丕尔-沃尔夫假说与语言相对论争论的核心。然而，共享的基本意义并不一定意味着它们之间的关系也相同。我们比较了81种语言中196个基本概念之间的关系，使用来自两个多语言模型的词嵌入来量化语言所表达的概念结构。研究发现，社会文化意义方面的跨语言一致性高于有关自然和运动的意义，这一对比在不同模型和分类体系中反复出现。在社会文化领域内，关系差异随地理距离的增加而增大；亲缘关系较远的语言在所有领域中差异更大。这些发现表明，普遍性与相对性在概念领域中相互交织。研究结果支持这样一种解释：共享的认知资源与语言和地理环境相互作用。
tldr: 本研究通过比较81种语言中196个基本概念的词嵌入发现，社会文化意义跨语言高度趋同而自然与运动意义分歧更大，揭示了概念结构中普遍性与语言相对性的交织。
en_tdlr: By comparing word embeddings of 196 basic concepts across 81 languages, this study shows that sociocultural meanings converge across languages more than meanings of nature and motion, revealing that universality and linguistic relativity are interwoven in conceptual structure.
